terra.problem: The statement that David was an earlier king of Israel is a Bible fact outside this passage and needs a reference.
Calling Saul Israel's first king states a Bible fact outside this passage without a reference.
Calling Jeroboam a king of Israel states a Bible fact outside this passage without a reference.
The closing lines are generic encouragement rather than Papa Dorin's distinctive voice.
The last two sentences restate the materials in a flat, generic way. A lively moment about the repair supplies is missed.
The explanation is flat and repetitive, ending with a list of materials already given in the quote.
Saying Josiah signs off on everything adds a claim about his authority that the passage does not give.
Saying the find changes the whole kingdom goes beyond this passage and gives away what happens later in the story.
Calling the ark a holy thing states a Bible fact outside this passage without a reference.
The statement about the bronze serpent being from Israel's past needs a reference outside this passage.
Josiah names the fathers' disobedience to the book as the reason for the LORD's wrath, not the book itself.
Huldah delivers the LORD's message to the men; they, not Huldah, bring the answer back to the king.
Calling it a gentle ending for Josiah goes beyond the promise that he will be gathered to his grave in peace. The passage does not describe how he dies.
Saying Josiah is not the one who sees the calamity removes the text's qualification: his eyes will not see all the calamity.
